reviewer: Opus session (D10): 4 independent Opus reviewers + adjudication

findings.note: Para B-33 defines the NFA and then says 'There are two exceptions': (1) 'When the establishing HQ approves joint fires within the NFA on a mission-by-mission basis' and (2) 'When an enemy force within the NFA engages a friendly force and the engaged commander determines there is a requirement for immediate protection and responds with the minimal force needed to defend the force.' On a 'What this means for you' takeaway slide the item reads as an absolute rule to act on; a Soldier engaged from inside an NFA would believe no fires are ever allowed. This is the rubric's own example of a major omission.
findings.fix: Now: 'prohibited, with two narrow exceptions (see the no-fire area slide)'.

findings.note: Para 3-29: danger close 'is a mandatory call alerting of an elevated risk to the closest friendly troops ... This is included with the method of engagement when the predicted impact ... is within 600 meters (m) of friendly troops for mortars or artillery'. The slide defines danger close as the rounds themselves and drops that it is a mandatory call, which is the action a Soldier takes. Numbers are correct and slide s13 covers the rest, so not major.
findings.fix: Now: 'Danger close is a mandatory call when mortar or artillery rounds are predicted to land within 600 meters of friendly troops.'

findings.note: Cites only list items para-1-28.li1-li3 ('C2 (...)', 'TA.', 'Attack/delivery systems.'). Nothing in the cited text says these are 'the fire support system's elements'; that comes from the lead-in para-1-28 ('The FS system elements ... are:'), which is not cited (planner.md §0 rule 2). Content itself is correct.
findings.fix: Now: 'The fire support system's elements: command and control, target acquisition, and attack/delivery systems.' (cites para-1-28, para-1-28.li1, para-1-28.li2, para-1-28.li3)

findings.note: Cited text 'Train and enforce task standards.' (para-1-47.li3) does not say who does this; attribution to NCOs rests on the uncited lead-in para-1-47 ('Noncommissioned officers:'). Attribution is correct in the doc tree.
findings.fix: Now: 'Train and enforce task standards.' (cites para-1-47, para-1-47.li3)

findings.note: Same as duties[1]: 'Continually focus training on sustaining strengths and improving weaknesses.' (para-1-47.li4) depends on the uncited lead-in para-1-47 for the NCO attribution.
findings.fix: Now: 'Keep training focused on sustaining strengths and improving weaknesses.' (cites para-1-47, para-1-47.li4)

findings.note: Source must-sentence: 'The FO must fully understand their responsibility within the observation plan and provide refinement or submit key targets for inclusion in the company fire plan.' The slide keeps 'must' but states only the first half, dropping the second required action. Not wrong, but the FO's full requirement is cut.
findings.fix: Now: 'The FO must fully understand their part in the observation plan and refine or submit key targets for the company fire plan.'

findings.note: Source: 'A joint fires observer cannot perform terminal attack control of CAS missions and does not replace a qualified joint terminal attack controller (JTAC) or forward air controller (airborne)'. 'Cannot control close air support attacks' is broader than 'terminal attack control' and sits beside the same para's statement that a JFO 'provides targeting information in support of close air support' (not on slide). Also drops 'qualified' and FAC(A). A Soldier would act about the same, so minor.
findings.fix: Now: 'Cannot perform terminal attack control of close air support; does not replace a qualified joint terminal attack controller (JTAC).'

findings.note: Para 2-38 says 'The BCT FSE works closely with BN FSEs and company FIST.' The slide flips the subject so the FIST works closely with battalion and brigade FSEs; the cited text does not state a FIST-to-battalion-FSE link (that comes from the BCT FSE working with both). Close, but not what the source says.
findings.fix: Now: 'The brigade fire support element works closely with battalion fire support elements and company FISTs.'

findings.note: Source: danger close 'is included with the method of engagement when the predicted impact of a round or shell is within 600 meters (m) of friendly troops for mortars or artillery'. Label drops 'predicted' and does not say this is the trigger for the danger close call; on a 'distances to know' slide a Soldier could read 600 m as a safe distance (the slide's own note warns not to confuse it with minimum safe distances).
findings.fix: Label now 'Mortar or artillery rounds predicted to land this close'; title 'Danger close: when to call it'.

findings.note: Same as s13.stats[0]: source says 'predicted impact ... within ... 750 m for naval surface fires'; label drops 'predicted' and the danger-close trigger framing.
findings.fix: Label now 'Naval surface fires predicted to land this close'.

findings.note: Rests on garbled table 3-1 ('Decide Mission Analysis ... Begin identifying high-payoff targets based on initial high-value target...'); alignment is plausible but not certain. 'High-payoff targets' is jargon not explained. Decide also covers developing the high-payoff target list, target selection standards and attack guidance matrix, so 'start identifying' is a narrow summary. Accepted: the Decide/Detect/Deliver step texts rest on table 3-1, which is garbled in the conversion; the adjudicator checked the cell alignment against the table text (Decide row: 'Begin identifying high-payoff targets...') and it matches. Term 'high-payoff targets' left as written; a plainer gloss would need text the source doesn't give here.
findings.fix: 'Decide: Pick the targets that matter most (high-payoff targets) and plan how to attack them.' Cite para-3-31 and table-3-1; or keep wording but add a one-line definition of high-payoff target from the doc tree.

findings.note: Slide-level framing: the checklist items para-3-51.li1-li5 are governed by 'For positive clearance of fires, the following should be obtained' (and li3 'if possible'). On the slide they sit under the title 'what it takes' directly after a 'must' item, with the 'should' only in speaker notes, so a reader could take the list as mandatory. Applies to items[2]-[6] and the title.
findings.fix: Added the source's lead-in as an item: 'For positive clearance of fires, the following should be obtained:' (directive should); title now 'what to get'; the battle-drill should moved to the notes.

findings.note: Source para A-7: 'The internal format for the fires paragraph ... Within each phase of an operation, each EFST will be described in the sequence of planned execution...'. The note drops 'within each phase of an operation' and that this is about how the fires paragraph is written.
findings.fix: Now: 'Within each phase of an operation, each essential fire support task will be described in the order of planned execution: task, purpose, method, effects.'

findings.note: Para B-33: NFA prohibits fires 'There are two exceptions.' The slide states the prohibition flat. This slide defines rather than tells the Soldier how to act, and s20 gives both exceptions, so minor rather than major.
findings.fix: Now: 'No-fire area: fires or their effects are prohibited inside it, with two exceptions.'

findings.note: Para B-2 says twice that the CFL 'does not eliminate the responsibility to coordinate the airspace required to conduct the mission'. The row says surface fires 'may fire beyond it at any time without more coordination' and only adds ROE, dropping the airspace-coordination condition. A Soldier could conclude no coordination at all is needed beyond a CFL, which is a safety risk for aircraft. Also drops 'law-of-war targeting constraints' and narrows 'conventional surface-to-surface direct fire and indirect fire support means' to 'surface fires' (acceptable).
findings.fix: Third cell now: 'Airspace still has to be coordinated; fires must follow rules of engagement.'

findings.note: Para B-33.li2: 'the engaged commander determines there is a requirement for immediate protection'. 'its commander' is ambiguous (could read as the enemy's or the NFA's commander) and 'need' drops that the engaged commander makes the determination. The outcome o2 'respond with only the minimal force' then lacks a subject, so it could read as permission for any unit.
findings.fix: Now: 'Enemy inside engages friendlies: does the engaged commander find protection is needed now?'

findings.note: Para E-1 gives two triggers: targets needing effects exceeding organic capabilities 'or when other requirements for joint airpower are identified during the planning process'. The step gives only the first, which could read as the only trigger. Not safety-relevant for the audience.
findings.fix: Now: 'Find a need for air support When targets need effects beyond the unit's own capabilities, or other joint air needs are found, the fire support element makes a request.'

findings.note: Cites only the footnote node para-4-62.t1 ('Note: (2). If designated by the support commander.'), which on its own does not say what it attaches to; the attachment comes from table-4-1, which is not cited. In table 4-1 the superscript 2 is on 'FA HQ' (DS, R, GSR rows) AND on 'FFA HQ' (GS row, and the 'positioned by'/'fires planned by' cells). The note names only 'Field artillery HQ', while the slide's GS row shows 'force field artillery HQ', which carries the same footnote. 'on the list only if' is a fair plain reading of the bare footnote, so no action changes, but the scope is incomplete.
findings.fix: Now: 'The field artillery HQ (and the force field artillery HQ for general support) is on the list only if designated by the support commander.' (cites para-4-62.t1, table-4-1)

findings.note: Source: 'FA personnel will use the M2A2 aiming circle to perform directional control in a GPS degraded, disrupted, or denied environment.' The note narrows the condition of a 'will' to 'Without GPS', which a listener could take to mean only when GPS is fully lost, not when it is degraded or disrupted. The directive word is kept; the trigger condition is narrowed.
findings.fix: Now: 'In a GPS degraded, disrupted, or denied environment, field artillery personnel will use the M2A2 aiming circle for directional control.'

findings.note: Cited ch-5.t1 says only: 'Section I discusses FS activities during competition. Section II discusses FS activities during crisis. This chapter ends with the transition to armed conflict.' 'before a war starts' is not in the cited text, and para 5-10 says crisis activities 'may also occur during conflict to prevent further escalation', so the framing over-claims slightly. The same framing is in the s29 title ('before the fighting').
findings.fix: Now: 'Fire support during competition and during crisis, and the move to armed conflict.'

findings.note: Source para D-141 is scoped to close air support: 'The following are considerations in the use of CAS in cold weather operations: ... Panels or pyrotechnics must be used to indicate friendly locations.' The note drops the CAS condition and states a 'must' for all cold-weather operations, so a Soldier could mark friendly positions with panels/pyrotechnics when no CAS is involved, which the publication does not require. Cite also omits the lead-in paragraph (planner rule 2).
findings.fix: Now: 'When close air support is used in cold weather, panels or pyrotechnics must be used...'; cites para-D-141 too.

findings.note: The 'must' sits in para 6-103, 'Plan fires to support the commitment of the reserve during movement. Fires are planned: ... FSCMs such as CFLs must be well forward to ensure the force will not outrun them.' The slide states it as a general offense rule and cites only the list item. Para 6-78 (same column) says 'The CFL should be planned as close as possible to the FLOT without restricting the maneuver operations', so the broadened 'must' also sits in tension with that general guidance.
findings.fix: Scoped to 'When the reserve is committed during movement'; cites para-6-103 and its li7.

findings.note: The cell says 'heat waves hamper distance estimates' but drops the requirement in the cited text that answers it: para D-101 'Laser range finders must be used, especially when heat waves degrade distance estimating by other conventional means.' The row above (s33.rows[1]) describes observing without a laser rangefinder, so a reader could take estimating by eye as normal in the desert.
findings.fix: Cell now: 'Heat waves hamper distance estimates: laser range finders must be used'.

findings.note: Lists white phosphorous as an effective munition in deep snow without its caution. Para D-136.li4: 'White phosphorous is effective; however, phosphorus may burn undetected in the snow for up to four days and may be a hazard to friendly troops subsequently moving through the area.' The caution is on s34.items[0], so it isn't lost from the deck, but this cell shows WP as simply effective.
findings.fix: Now: 'Deep snow (cold weather) Airburst munitions; white phosphorous (may burn undetected for 4 days) High explosives (HE) point detonating or delay: ineffective in deep snow Amber filters cut snow blindness; update visibility diagrams regularly'

findings.note: 'Meet the five requirements for accurate predicted fire for first-round fire for effect' is jargon a junior Soldier can't apply: the five requirements are never named, and 'predicted fire' and 'fire for effect' aren't explained. The framing 'To surprise the enemy, ...' also gives one of the four ways para 6-86 lists ('Commanders can use FS to achieve surprise by: ...'), not the only one.
findings.fix: Now: 'To help surprise the enemy, meet the five requirements for accurate predicted fire so the first rounds are fire for effect.'

findings.note: Drops the purpose clause from para-6-128.li3 'Smoke should be used with fog or darkness to maximize effectiveness.' Without it, the slide can read as a condition on when smoke is used at all. Also cuts the friendly-side drawback from li5: 'Smoke may attract enemy attention or degrade friendly TA or control.'
findings.fix: Now: 'Obscure Reduce enemy direct fire on the breach. Smoke should be used with fog or darkness to maximize effect; it may attract enemy attention.'

findings.note: Glossary definition ends '...from the intended point of a weapon's impact requiring specific procedures for risk mitigation.' The slide says 'from where a weapon impacts' (loses 'intended') and drops that the call requires specific risk-mitigation procedures, which is the practical point on a safety term.
findings.fix: Now: 'A mandatory call that warns of higher risk to the closest friendly troops from a weapon's intended point of impact. It requires specific risk-mitigation procedures.'

deck_notes: [reviewer A] s01 (title slide) has no claims in the packet; its title/subtitle are fine.

[reviewer A] s03 is framed 'What this means for you', so its items read as action rules; that framing is why the NFA exception omission (s03.items[3]) is major. s20 covers NFA exceptions later, but s03 should not state the rule as absolute.
[reviewer A] s02.stats[2] gives 600 m for mortars/artillery only, which matches para 3-29; 750 m naval is omitted, acceptable for an at-a-glance stat with the label scoped to mortars/artillery.
[reviewer A] Acronyms on s09-s10 (FO, FSO, FIST, JTAC) are spelled out via role names/titles; 'troop' on s09/s10 is unexplained Army jargon for a cavalry company but harmless.
[reviewer A] No NOT FOUND IN DECK markers in s02-s11.

[reviewer B] s13 is the highest-risk slide in this range: big numbers under 'the distances to know' invite reading 600/750 m as safe distances. Talking point [2] covers this only in the notes; consider putting 'not a minimum safe distance' on the slide.
[reviewer B] s14 steps describe staff targeting work (high-payoff target lists, attack guidance matrix); low relevance to junior Soldiers but faithful except as noted.

[reviewer B] s18 places 'Fires must be cleared with both terrain owners and other airspace users' (para B-1) next to the free-fire area 'without more coordination' item; both are faithful, but the integrator may want the instructor note to explain the difference.
[reviewer B] s20 tree edges checked in the spec: q1 yes->o1, no->q2; q2 yes->o2, no->o3. Logic matches para B-33.
[reviewer B] s19 FSCL row checked against the column header 'Beyond or across the line'; reads correctly.

[reviewer C] s24 (table 4-1, garbled in source): checked every 'answers calls for fire' cell against the cited table text. DS, R and GSR priorities are read correctly from clean cells. The GS cell is truncated ('1. Supported unit 2.FFA HQ 3. Own'), and the slide correctly stops at 'then others (see table 4-1)' without guessing 'own observers'. No cell is guessed. The table's 'in priority' wording became 'then ...', which keeps the order.

[reviewer C] s29 title 'Fire support before the fighting: competition and crisis' has the same slight over-claim as s28.blurb: para 5-10 says crisis activities 'may also occur during conflict'. Consider 'Fire support in competition and crisis'.

[reviewer C] s27: the source labels para-C-32.t2/t3 as a CAUTION (para-C-32.t1). The slide's 'Don't' items carry the content faithfully. Consider having the renderer or title mark it as a CAUTION so the safety status is visible. All directive words (must never, should, may, will) and numbers (3 to 6 inches) are exact.

[reviewer C] s26: the pivot step and the hole step are alternatives in para C-11 ('Alternatively, the receiver can be placed in a hole'). The process_flow arrows suggest a sequence, but the 'Or' label on step 4 makes the alternative clear enough. Numbers (90 degrees, two minutes, six inches) are exact.

[reviewer C] s25: 'may be necessary' (voice) is a possibility, not a permission, and the slide keeps that sense. 'Missions from untrained observers must be rehearsed during training' sits under 'Voice', which matches the context of para 4-88.

[reviewer D] s32.steps[0] and s32.steps[1] contain directive words (must; should, may) but carry no 'directive' field in the packet header ('words:' only). This is fine for meaning, but plan --check and the spec metadata won't record the must in steps[0].

[reviewer D] s31.columns[0] draws on 'FS preparation considerations' (para 6-44) and 'FS considerations' (6-41), which are planning items for FS staff, not individual Soldier tasks. That's fine for context, but the slide shouldn't be framed as what the viewer must do.

[reviewer D] s34 mixes continuous-operations content (para D-134 sleep rule, a speaker note) into a terrain/weather hazards slide. It's accurate, but the note should say it comes from continuous operations, not a terrain or weather hazard.
[reviewer D] s33/s34 keep the source spelling 'phosphorous' in s33 and use 'phosphorus' in s34; harmless, but make them consistent.

[reviewer D] Verified section context in data/md/FM-3-09.md: D-76 is in Section IV Jungle, D-65/66/70 Mountain, D-99 to D-113 Desert, D-136 to D-144 Cold Weather (D-141 is the CAS subsection), D-16/17/26/28/41 Urban. 6-78 and 6-103 are in Section IV The Offense.

[adjudicator] All 5 critical/major findings confirmed against the source and fixed: cold-weather CAS 'must' (D-141) scoped to CAS; coordinated-fire-line 'must' (6-103) scoped to committing the reserve; desert laser rangefinder 'must' (D-101) restored; CFL airspace duty (B-2) restored; no-fire-area takeaway now flags its exceptions.
[adjudicator] After fixes: plan --check 0 errors / 0 warnings; deck re-rendered (37 slides); every on-slide claim found in the rendered deck text.

[adjudicator] Not changed (planning-level, for WP 4.4): s31's defense column is staff planning content; s07 'Who trains you' is training, not fires; the s27 sun-filter caution isn't marked CAUTION on the slide (renderer could add a caution style); s33/s34 spell 'phosphorous'/'phosphorus' as each source line does.
